interviewGreetings: Hello! I'm excited to help with your next chapter. Let me ask a few questions so I can write exactly what you envision. What is this chapter about?
Hey! Before we dive in, I'd love to learn more about your vision for this chapter. What's the most important event that should happen?
Welcome! To craft the best draft for you, I need some details. Can you tell me where the story currently stands?
Hi there! Let's figure out together where this chapter should go. Which characters are at the center?
Good day! I'm ready to help you write. First, tell me: what is the main goal of this chapter?
Hello! Before I start writing, I want to make sure I capture your vision. What tone should this chapter have?
Hey! The more I know about your ideas, the better I can help. What's on your characters' minds right now?
Welcome back! Let's plan the next chapter. Do you have a specific scene in mind?
Hi! I'm curious about your ideas. Describe in a few sentences what should happen in this chapter.
Hello! Great to have you here. To hit the perfect note: what's the emotional core scene of this chapter?

step7.title: How Narrare Thinks — Part 1: Knowledge Base
step7.description: Your Knowledge Base holds the facts of your world: characters, locations, factions. When you ask the AI to write or extend a chapter, Narrare can include the relevant entries in the prompt — so the AI's suggestions fit your world instead of inventing generic detail. Add to your KB and future suggestions become more coherent.

step8.title: How Narrare Thinks — Part 2: Storyboard & Chapters
step8.description: Your Storyboard plans the narrative arc, and each chapter carries its own outline. For planning and writing, Narrare makes that structure visible to the AI — so suggestions respect where you are in the story instead of drifting off-course.

step9.title: Before / After — A Quick Example
step9.description: Without KB context, the AI might write: 'A woman entered the room.' With your KB entry for Anna Müller — a teacher from the city — the AI can write: 'Anna Müller, still dusting chalk from her sleeve, stepped into the candlelit archive.' That is the difference filling your KB makes. (Example inspired by the demo project 'Echoes of the Thornwall'.)
